chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zayd al-Shahham who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of al-Maghrib. So he said: 'Jibrail (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) with two times for every salat, except for al-Maghrib salat — for its time is one, and its time is when it becomes obligatory.'

key_terms.المغرب: Al-Maghrib — the sunset prayer, the fourth of the five daily prayers
key_terms.وقتها وجوبها: Its time is its obligatory time — a technical jurisprudential phrase stating that for Maghrib, the prescribed window and the obligatory deadline are the same point
key_terms.وقتين: Two times — referring to the early recommended time and the later time (the extended window) assigned to each prayer by Jibrail

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the time of Maghrib prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains to Zayd al-Shahham that while Jibrail (Gabriel) brought two designated times for each daily prayer — an earlier recommended time and a later time marking the end of the window — the Maghrib prayer is unique in having only a single time. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential position that Maghrib's time begins immediately at sunset and the prayer should be performed promptly; its time is its obligation, meaning the moment it is due, it is obligatory and the ideal time coincides with the obligatory time.
